title: Chapter 23: A Temporary Contract
content:
Chapter 23:

A Temporary Contract

Driving even Emilia out of his room, Subaru’s fourth loop got off to a bleak start.

On the morning of the first day, after hurting Emilia with a heartless remark, a confrontation with the returned Roswaal awaited him.

His mocking attitude hadn’t changed, but Subaru felt ill at ease, feeling as though he were being looked upon with appraising eyes. Whether that was limited to this time around, or if it had been the same in the previous loops, the Subaru of now had no way of knowing.

Their conversation was brief, and its contents barely remained in his memory.

He only vaguely felt he’d received words to the effect that he would be treated as a guest.

He also felt like Roswaal had said something convenient, like he should stay as long as he pleased.

That could be said to be a wish come true for Subaru, but it could also be said to be a matter that was already of no importance.

If he wandered out of the mansion now, he would surely be killed to silence him. Yet, even if he stayed and was judged as nothing but baggage for the Roswaal camp, it was obvious that a future where he was turned into mincemeat awaited him before long.

To leave is a 

BAD END

; to stay is a 

BAD END

.

It felt like he had saved in a position where the approaching 

BAD END

 could not be avoided. Even though it was an auto-save, what an absurd setup this was.

While spouting such curses, Subaru spent the day crouching in a corner of the room, idling the time away. Since coming to this parallel world, this was likely the first day he had done so little.

Come to think of it, the current Subaru was in the position of the “kept man” he had longed for. Meals were served without him working, and no one complained even if he holed up in his room.

Despite being in a parallel world, he was leading the same shut-in life as he had in his original world. That should have been what he looked forward to, yet he felt not a speck of deep emotion for the time he had so craved.

Unable to even choose the attractive option of indulging in lazy slumber, Subaru could not even sleep on the guest room bed, spending his idleness holding his head in his hands.

In his hand, he gripped a quill pen in a reverse hold; its tip was stained with blood that had been dipped into and dried countless times. Whenever he lost to drowsiness and his eyelids began to droop, he stabbed the back of his hand, forcibly bringing his consciousness to an awake state through pain.

Though he barely moved atop the bed, breathing through his mouth, Subaru’s breaths were rough and rapid. His heart continued to beat fast and short in unbroken tension, and his eyes darted about, captive to paranoia, constantly doubting if there were any abnormalities in the room.

He had already died three times, and his days at the Roswaal manor were entering their fourth iteration.

In Subaru’s experience, his death count as of the first day of summoning had been three. For Subaru, who had broken through that day on the fourth attempt, a fourth death was unknown territory.

—If he died here and now, he might not be able to come back next time.

He could find no method to avoid death. Even so, he did not want to die.

But living here was also so painful and agonizing that he could hardly bear it. All that Subaru, who felt like he was losing his mind, could do was choose a conclusion that made it seem like he had lost his mind.

Namely: to doubt everything, to resist everything, and to cling single-mindedly to life.

He had already entered the afternoon of the second day of the fourth loop; the time he had spent in idleness was too different from the previous repetitions, so his memories from before were no longer reliable.

He didn’t know what would happen, and it wouldn’t be strange for anything to happen. And even if something did happen, it would all surely be to Subaru’s disadvantage.

Disappointed in reality, despairing at the situation, and resigned to the future, Subaru’s heart had broken and shattered.

Now, only the remnants of it continued a disgraceful, futile struggle.

Unable to perceive day as day or night as night, even the passage of time became vague, and the boundary between consciousness and unconsciousness wavered like a heat haze.

Only the pain of stabbing the back of his hand was vivid; the fact that the sensation was so sharp made him just a little happy, and he gouged the wound again and again. Gouge. Gouge. Gouge.

“—You’re wearing quite the spineless look on your face, I suppose.”

Suddenly hearing that voice, he raised his head as if he’d been struck.

At the end of Subaru’s beast-like, glaring gaze, gripping the doorknob and leaning toward him, was the girl he had not yet met even once in this loop.

Beatrice’s visit—it was a first within the four repeated worlds. And Subaru instantly heightened his vigilance.

An abnormality that could only occur this time—it was bound to lead directly to a result that threatened Subaru’s life.

“…So this time, it’s you.”

A low, hoarse voice came out, surprising even himself.

His throat, which had remained silent for over two days and had only passed rough breaths, was parched and raw. It contained more hostility than he had intended, and the girl who received that malice head-on said,

“How can one rot so much in just a day or two, I wonder? Humans are hopelessly foolish creatures, in fact.”

“I’ve got no intention of listening to your lecture. —What did you come here for?”

Beatrice laughed scornfully at Subaru’s shameful state. She furrowed her brows in displeasure at Subaru’s way of speaking, which lacked any tact, and said,

“Bubby and that little girl told me to, so I came to see your face, in fact.”

“Puck and… Emilia?”

“Since you’ve been acting strange since you woke up, they suspect Betty might have done something when you first woke up, in fact. It’s a rude story, I suppose.”

Emilia, who should have been hurt by Subaru’s heartless words, was even now worrying about Subaru’s heart. She had thought the cause of Subaru’s change might be Beatrice, whom he had contacted just before, and had appealed directly to Beatrice.

Beatrice, who for some reason could not stand up to Puck, had been supported by Puck—who was overly soft on his daughter—and had thus reluctantly shown her face at Subaru’s place.

Emilia’s concern—it left a warmth, however slight, in Subaru’s desolate heart. However, her worry was grossly misplaced.

The cause of Subaru’s sudden change was unrelated to Beatrice, and this was not a problem that could be solved no matter what anyone did for him anymore.

“I get it. That’s enough. I understand what you’re saying, so just get lost. You came to apologize. That’s enough.”

“Why must Betty apologize, I wonder? Unless we start by correcting that, I can’t go back even if I wanted to, in fact.”

Beatrice pressed on as Subaru waved his hand, trying to drive her away roughly. Then she stepped further into the room, moving as she dragged the hem of her long skirt, and…

“—Ugh?”

Suddenly, she wrinkled her nose and stopped.

Her profile, which would be adorable if she kept silent, turned its neck like a dog tracking a scent, sniffing around the area.

Eventually, she glared at Subaru, her eyes harboring grand displeasure, and said,

“Not only has your face become gloomy, but it’s become quite thick, in fact.”

“—Huh?”

“I’m talking about the smell, I suppose. It stinks; it’s the worst scent, in fact. It would be wise not to meet those twins for a while, I suppose.”

Beatrice pinched her nose and waved her hand to emphasize the stench.

Not even noticing her gesture, Subaru’s thoughts turned to a memory corresponding to the keyword “smell.”

The smell, surely that was what someone said when the third loop ended—

“What do you say smells on me?”

Raising his head, Subaru asked the question, imbuing his voice with the color of emotion for the first time.

At the question, Beatrice raised one eyebrow, crossed her arms, and said,

“It’s the smell of the Witch, in fact. It’s enough to make my nose crooked, I suppose.”

Muttering the keyword “Witch,” a corner of his mind suddenly began to throb.

He remembered that word. He should have seen that word just recently. That was—

“The Witch of Envy.”

“In this current world, when one says Witch, What else could one mean, I wonder?”

At Beatrice’s mocking manner of speech, Subaru instinctively leaned forward. Reaching his hand out toward her, he asked,

“Why are you smelling that from me?”

“Who knows? Maybe the Witch took a fancy to you, or maybe she made you her enemy. Either way, you receiving special treatment from the Witch makes you a nuisance, in fact.”

“Being given special treatment by someone whose face and name I don’t know gives me the creeps.”

Beatrice shrugged, her attitude implicitly showing that even discussing it further was unpleasant. At her stubborn stance of refusal, Subaru shut his mouth and began to dive into the sea of thought while organizing the current fragments of information.

The Witch. The Witch of Envy was a globally famous figure remaining in fairy tales, hated and feared by the entire world, whose name everyone avoided even mentioning.

The only knowledge Subaru possessed regarding her existence was what was told in stories that lacked even a story.

Naturally, he had no memory of meeting her, nor did he recall having any contact with her whatsoever.

It was an absurd story that the lingering scent of the Witch would stain him when he hadn’t even experienced such a thing.

—I feel like Rem said something like that to me, too.

If a part of her excessive murderous intent lay in that, then Subaru had once again bought resentment for a fact he had no recollection of. Since all his crimes were false accusations, Subaru’s bad luck in being killed repeatedly was truly top-tier.

Realizing that helpless facts were simply helpless, Subaru let out a long sigh of fatigue. Seeing that, and perhaps judging there would be no further development in the conversation, Beatrice smoothed down her long hair with her hand and said,

“If there’s nothing else, I will be going, in fact. I will properly tell Bubby that Betty came to see you, I suppose.”

“Wait a sec.”

He called out to her back as she reached for the doorknob to perform “Door Crossing,” stopping her movement. To Beatrice, who looked back at him only with her neck,

“You feel bad for me, don’t you?”

Subaru threw the question at her maliciously.

It was a move that might be somewhat of a gamble, but he followed his heart’s plea that it was better than doing nothing.

To Beatrice, who wore a look of disgust, Subaru tapped the sheets lightly and asked again,

“You. Feel. Bad. For. Me. Answer Yes or No.”

“I don’t, in fact.”

“I’m telling Puck.”

“Gh… I might occasionally think so just a liiiiittle bit, I suppose.”

Turning her whole body back toward Subaru, Beatrice crossed her arms and looked away haughtily.

Looking at her small body from top to bottom, and then recalling the time he had spent with her until now—Subaru agonized over it, then made a decision.

“If you want me to forgive you, listen to just one request.”

That was—

“One night… no, until the morning after next is fine. Can you protect me?”

It was nothing other than a truly shameless choice, to beg a girl who looked younger than himself.

Beatrice fell silent for a moment at the request Subaru had broached, and said,

“That’s a vague way of putting it, in fact. Is there a reason you’re being targeted, I wonder?”

She returned a perfectly natural question.

Beatrice began to walk around the room while looking coldly at Subaru, and said,

“In the first place, I want no part of trouble being brought into this mansion. This mansion is an indispensable place for Betty, I suppose.”

“…I don’t intend to start anything myself. I just want to brush away the sparks falling on me.”

“For leaving even that to others, that’s quite the noble ambition, in fact.”

“Just this time, I’ve got no comeback.”

Beatrice sighed at the downcast Subaru.

For a while, a time of silence flowed through the room.

Head still down, Subaru thought he would hear the sound of the door closing before long. The sound of Beatrice casting aside his plea and fluttering back to her Forbidden Library.

When he heard that, it would be the moment even the single drop of hope Subaru had managed to connect with would be crushed.

To Subaru, filled with such resignation,

“Put out your hand, in fact.”

Beatrice had walked up to the side of the bed and was holding her small hand out toward him.

Subaru was taken aback. She impatiently took Subaru’s right hand, looked at the scar-covered back of it, grimaced, and said,

“Disgusting. To think you even have a habit of self-harm, you’re a hopeless pervert, I suppose.”

“That is Roswaal’s identity… I’m just a delusional teenager with a bit too much youth leaking out.”

“I don’t understand what you mean, but I know your hopelessness has only deepened, I suppose.”

Sighing, Beatrice turned Subaru’s right hand palm up to hide the wounds, and placed her own small palm over it.

Naturally, as if invited, they clasped hands, fingers intertwining with fingers, and…

“—I shall heed thy wish. In the name of Beatrice, the contract is hereby sealed.”

Subaru was lost for words at the sight of Beatrice speaking so solemnly.

And then, an overwhelming heat transmitted from their intertwined palms. It traveled through his palm to spread throughout Subaru’s entire body, suddenly shocking vitality into his drained frame.

Bewildered by his body’s sudden heated reaction, he looked forward to see Beatrice glaring at him with eyes that seemed to say she was thoroughly reluctant, saying,

“Even if it is temporary, a contract is a contract. Formed in accordance with the ritual, it is absolute, in fact. I will listen to your incomprehensible request, I suppose.”

“You should be grateful”—concluding with that, Beatrice stared boldly at Subaru with a superior gaze, despite looking from below.

Receiving that gaze, Subaru instantly looked away, trying to endure a wave of inexplicable emotion that suddenly visited him.

A welling passion, a sensation beyond words.

Not knowing how to handle that, extended from such an unexpected place, Subaru closed his eyes to the heat of the palm being held, and said,

“For real…? I almost got made to cry by a loli.”

“Don’t call me a loli, in fact. —Also, if you tattle to Bubby, I will absolutely not forgive you, I suppose.”

“You’re so desperate. That’s seriously demonic.”

Being on the receiving end of a gaze filled with genuine hostility, Subaru responded with a bitter smile.

It was the first smile, however small but certain, to appear in this fourth loop.
